admission_type.route_name: Selection for the Master's Degree Programmes in Finance and Management — GMAT/GRE certification route (EU/Schengen applicants)
admission_type.eligible_applicants: EU/Schengen citizens who have completed, or are about to complete, a Bachelor's degree (Italian or foreign) that qualifies them to enrol in an Italian Master's degree in Management or Finance
admission_type.test_or_certification: GMAT with a minimum score of 555 (out of 805) OR GRE with a minimum score of 157 (out of 170) in BOTH the Quantitative and Verbal sections. These thresholds are specific to Finance and Management and are higher than the general Luiss certification route (GMAT >= 515 / GRE >= 154). The Luiss Test (Luiss EU Test) does NOT apply to this programme: Finance does not appear in the list of programmes selectable via the Luiss Test, nor in the list for the general GMAT/GRE certification route; Finance and Management have their own dedicated selection page.
admission_type.number_of_choices_allowed: 1 [uncertain: the Finance/Management selection page does not state a number explicitly; the parallel EU and non-EU certification pages both state "You can apply for only one of the available Master's degree courses", and the Finance/Management page describes a single chosen degree programme that can be changed only by written request to ammissione@luiss.it]
admission_type.choice_is_binding: true [uncertain: the Finance/Management page does not repeat the binding wording, but the parallel certification pages state "your course choice is binding for admission, ranking, and subsequent enrolment"; the Finance/Management page allows change requests only within the timeframes set in the Admission Notice]

admission_type.route_name: Luiss Test (Luiss EU Test) — NOT APPLICABLE to Finance
admission_type.eligible_applicants: Not applicable. Explicitly recorded here to make the exclusion unambiguous.
admission_type.test_or_certification: The Luiss Test is NOT an entry route to the Master's Degree in Finance. The Luiss Test page lists the selectable Economics-area programmes (Administration, Finance and Control; Economics, Institutions and Financial Markets; Marketing; Strategic Management; Data Science and Management; Global Management and Politics) — Finance and Management are absent. Finance and Management are handled exclusively through the dedicated GMAT/GRE selection page.

academic_requirements.prior_qualification: A completed (or about to be completed) three-year Bachelor's degree, obtained in Italy or abroad, that qualifies the holder to enrol in a Master's degree in Management or Finance in Italy. The Bachelor's degree must be obtained by 18 November 2027 for the 2027/2028 cycle.
academic_requirements.minimum_curricular_requirements: Per the Luiss "Minimum curricular requirements" page for the 2027/2028 academic year, Finance is grouped with Management, Strategic Management, Marketing and Amministrazione, Finanza e Controllo. Admission is open to students enrolled in or graduates of: L-18 (D.M. 270/04) and 17 (D.M. 509/99) – Economics and Business Management; L-33 (D.M. 270/04) and 28 (D.M. 509/99) – Economics. Students from other degree programmes may only be admitted if they have at least 24 university credits (ECTS) in total, already earned or still to be earned, in at least three of the following subject areas: Business (ECON-06/A; ECON-07/A; ECON-08/A; ECON-09/A; ECON-09/B); Economics (ECON-01/A; ECON-04/A); Statistics (STAT-01/A; STAT-02/A; STAT-03/A; STAT-04/A; MATH-03/A; MATH-03/B); Law (GIUR-01/A; GIUR-02/A; GIUR-03/A; GIUR-05/A; GIUR-06/A; GIUR-09/A; GIUR-10/A).
academic_requirements.minimum_grade_or_gpa: No general minimum grade for the GMAT/GRE route (the GMAT/GRE score is the threshold). For the Luiss internal direct-access route: weighted average of at least 28/30, without rounding, at the end of the 2026/2027 winter session.
academic_requirements.country_specific_rules: No Finance-specific country list is published. General rules apply: foreign qualifications must have been awarded on completion of a first-level programme of at least 3 (or 4) academic years, must grant access to graduate programmes in the awarding country, must be issued by an officially recognised university, and must not be a professional/vocational qualification. Where a system distinguishes Ordinary from Honours Bachelor's degrees, only Honours Bachelor's degrees qualify for admission to Italian Master's degrees.
academic_requirements.document_recognition: Enrolment with a foreign qualification is subject to validation by the Luiss Admissions Office. Accepted documentation depends on the country: Diploma Supplement for Lisbon Recognition Convention signatory countries; CIMEA Statement of Verification or an Apostille of the Diploma for countries included in the Automatic Recognition Database – Italy (ARDI); CIMEA Statement of Comparability or a Declaration of Value (DoV) issued by the competent Italian Embassy/Consulate for countries not in ARDI or the Lisbon Convention.
academic_requirements.compensatory_measures: None published for this Master's programme. Candidates who do not meet the minimum curricular requirements are simply not admitted; there is no published foundation-year or additional-credits remedy for master's entry. [uncertain: not explicitly denied on any page — absence of a published remedy]

entry_exam_or_test.test_name: GMAT or GRE (external standardised tests). There is NO Luiss admission test for the Master's Degree in Finance — the Luiss Test does not cover Finance or Management.
entry_exam_or_test.content: GMAT: overall score on the 805-point scale (minimum 555). GRE: Quantitative and Verbal sections, minimum 157 out of 170 in EACH of the two sections. Luiss does not itself set the test content — it is defined by GMAC (GMAT) and ETS (GRE).
entry_exam_or_test.format: Externally administered by GMAC/ETS (test-centre or at-home online options as offered by those providers). Luiss requires the certificate to be attached to the online application and the official score to be transmitted directly through the provider's platform. Applications are submitted through an online form; there are two separate forms, one for EU/Schengen and one for non-EU/non-Schengen applicants.
entry_exam_or_test.dates: No Luiss-administered test date. The GMAT/GRE must be sat independently and the score submitted within the application window (December 2026 – 31 March 2027 for 2027/2028). Deadlines for uploading the unofficial score and transmitting the official score are set in the Admission Notice (available from November 2026).
entry_exam_or_test.fee: Luiss participation fee: EUR 150 (mandatory, non-refundable). GMAT/GRE test fees are paid separately to GMAC/ETS and are not published by Luiss.
entry_exam_or_test.language_of_test: English (GMAT and GRE are English-language tests). The Luiss Test rule that an Italian-language test restricts applicants to Italian-taught programmes is irrelevant here, since the Luiss Test does not apply to Finance.
entry_exam_or_test.interview: No interview mentioned. Selection is documentary: "Candidates who meet the requirements are admitted directly to the Master's Degree Courses based on the international certification they submit" and a Committee reviews the documentation against the requirements and available places. [uncertain: wording quoted from the parallel EU certification page; the Finance/Management page does not describe an interview either]

The programme-specific page (EUR 17,000) is the more specific and more recently year-badged source (2027/2028) and is recorded as the primary figure, with EUR 18,000 recorded as the conflicting admission-FAQ figure. The research brief expected EUR 18,000. The EUR 17,000 figure comes from the programme-specific 2027/2028 page and is recorded as primary; the EUR 18,000 figure is recorded as the conflicting admission-FAQ value. Unresolved.

GARBLED SOURCE TEXT: The same admission FAQ sentence says "€18,000 for the Bachelor's degree programmes in Management and Finance", but Management and Finance are MASTER'S programmes at Luiss — this is evidently a translation error in the English version of the site, which further undermines the reliability of the EUR 18,000 figure.

ENGLISH CERTIFICATES UNVERIFIED: The brief's expected list (IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT 78-80, Cambridge FCE grade B / CAE grade C) could NOT be found on any current luiss.it Master's-degree admission page. Only "B2 level of English, which will be assessed during the admission test" appears, on the Minimum Curricular Requirements page. Web search returned IELTS/TOEFL thresholds only for Luiss Business School and Luiss School of Government programmes, which are different institutions/programmes and must not be applied to this LM-77 degree.

How B2 English is verified for GMAT/GRE-route Finance applicants is unspecified on any consulted page.

NUMBER OF CHOICES / BINDING NATURE INFERRED: The Finance/Management selection page does not state how many programmes may be selected or that the choice is binding. Both values were inferred from the parallel EU and non-EU general certification pages, which state one choice only and that the choice is binding. Treat as inferred, not verified for Finance specifically.

NON-EU CALENDAR INFERRED: The Finance/Management selection page presents one calendar described as "open to students from both within and outside the EU", while the extra-EU hub page separately says non-EU 2027/2028 procedures are "coming soon". The non-EU dates recorded here are therefore taken from the shared calendar and are not confirmed by a non-EU-specific notice.

RENAME/SUCCESSION UNVERIFIED: The brief states Finance is the successor to the former "Corporate Finance" and "Economics and Finance" programmes. The programme page never says this, but it does contain a stale sentence, "Admission to the Degree Course in Corporate Finance represents a unique opportunity...", which is circumstantial support. Not confirmed.
